items.followUp: Write any two industrial uses of enzymes.

rubric.why: One mark for a valid use of enzymes in digestion.
rubric.description: State that enzymes help digest food by breaking it into simpler substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining their role in digestion.

rubric.why: One mark for another valid use of enzymes.
rubric.description: Name a use of enzymes in industry, such as in detergents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct industrial use.

modelAnswer: Enzymes help digest food by breaking complex food substances into simpler substances.
Enzymes are used in industry, for example in detergents to remove stains.

items.followUp: Define optimum pH for an enzyme.

rubric.why: The definition must identify temperature as the condition being described.
rubric.description: Identify the temperature at which enzyme activity is being considered.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to temperature.

rubric.why: Optimum temperature is defined by the enzyme's highest activity or reaction rate.
rubric.description: State that the enzyme works at its maximum rate or activity at this temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum-activity idea.

modelAnswer: Optimum temperature is the temperature at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate or activity.

items.followUp: Differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Intracellular enzymes act within cells.
rubric.description: State where intracellular enzymes act.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating their action inside cells.

rubric.why: Extracellular enzymes act outside cells, usually after being secreted.
rubric.description: State where extracellular enzymes act.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating their action outside cells.

modelAnswer: Intracellular enzymes act inside the cells in which they are produced.
Extracellular enzymes are released from cells and act outside them.

rubric.why: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon-to-carbon double bonds.
rubric.description: State the type of bonds between the carbon atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the carbon chain has single bonds and no double bonds.

rubric.why: The single-bonded carbon chain holds the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms.
rubric.description: State that the fatty acid contains the maximum number of hydrogen atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum-hydrogen feature.

modelAnswer: Saturated fatty acids have carbon atoms joined only by single bonds, with no carbon-to-carbon double bonds.
Their carbon chains therefore carry the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms.

items.followUp: Which diseases are caused by a deficiency of vitamins A and B₁?

rubric.why: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.
rubric.description: Name the disease caused by vitamin C deficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for scurvy.

rubric.why: Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets.
rubric.description: Name the disease caused by vitamin D deficiency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for rickets.

modelAnswer: Deficiency of vitamin C causes scurvy.
Deficiency of vitamin D causes rickets.

items.followUp: Explain the cellular and organ levels of biological organization.

rubric.why: The molecular level begins with atoms combining to form molecules.
rubric.description: Explain how molecules form at the molecular level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms combine to form molecules.

rubric.why: Molecules are organized into cell structures such as organelles.
rubric.description: Describe the organization of molecules into cell structures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking molecules to organelles.

rubric.why: A tissue is made up of similar cells.
rubric.description: Identify the cellular composition of a tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a tissue consists of similar cells.

rubric.why: The cells in a tissue work together to perform a particular function.
rubric.description: State what the cells of a tissue do together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the shared-function idea.

modelAnswer: At the molecular level, atoms combine to form molecules such as water, proteins and lipids.
These molecules combine and are organized into cell structures called organelles.
A tissue is a group of similar cells, often with intercellular material, working together.
The cells of a tissue perform a particular function.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and function of the nucleus, with a labelled diagram.

rubric.why: A ribosome consists of a large and a small subunit.
rubric.description: Name both ribosomal subunits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both subunits are correctly identified.

rubric.why: Ribosomes are made of ribosomal RNA and proteins.
rubric.description: State the components of ribosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying RNA and protein as components.

rubric.why: Ribosomes are non-membranous cell structures.
rubric.description: State that ribosomes lack a surrounding membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the non-membranous feature.

rubric.why: The main function of ribosomes is protein synthesis.
rubric.description: State the function of ribosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for protein synthesis.

rubric.why: The diagram should represent and label the two subunits and the mRNA strand associated with the ribosome.
rubric.description: Draw a labelled ribosome diagram showing its subunits and mRNA.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a clear diagram with the large subunit, small subunit and mRNA labelled.

modelAnswer: A ribosome is a small, non-membranous cell structure made of ribosomal RNA and proteins.
It consists of a large subunit and a small subunit.
The two subunits come together during protein synthesis; ribosomes may be free in the cytoplasm or attached to rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.

Large subunit
Small subunit

items.followUp: Give one characteristic of each of the five kingdoms of organisms.

rubric.why: Monerans are prokaryotic and unicellular; protists are eukaryotic and mostly unicellular.
rubric.description: Give the characteristic cell type and organization of Monera and Protista.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing Monera and Protista.

rubric.why: Fungi are heterotrophic and commonly absorb nutrients; their cell walls contain chitin.
rubric.description: State a valid characteristic of fungi.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct fungal characteristic.

rubric.why: Plants are generally autotrophic and have cellulose cell walls.
rubric.description: State a valid characteristic of Plantae.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct plant characteristic.

rubric.why: Animals are multicellular heterotrophs and their cells lack cell walls.
rubric.description: State a valid characteristic of Animalia.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct animal characteristic.

modelAnswer: Monera: organisms are prokaryotic and unicellular.
Protista: organisms are eukaryotic and mostly unicellular.
Fungi: organisms are eukaryotic heterotrophs that absorb nutrients; their cell walls contain chitin.
Plantae: organisms are multicellular eukaryotes, generally autotrophic, with cellulose cell walls.
Animalia: organisms are multicellular eukaryotic heterotrophs whose cells lack cell walls.
